beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps dense image information in a carrier while a compact recurrent thought process updates it inside the flow.
beats.claim: ThinkSR runs end to end through encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, and decoder.
beats.narration: The method separates dense spatial storage from the compact process that reasons over it. The encoder creates the feature field that will carry image detail. Windowing prepares that field for token-wise processing without dropping it. The DQ-CTM thought stage is recurrent, and its parameters are shared across ticks. The decoder turns the updated carrier back into the super-resolution image.

params.headline: ThinkSR updates a dense carrier with shared DQ-CTM ticks
params.note: The recurrence stays inside the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines the dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into windows while retaining every token.
beats.narration: The carrier starts as an encoded version of the low-resolution input image. The encoder maps the image into a dense feature field. The low-resolution image is the input being lifted into that field. The window partition operates on the dense feature field and keeps the tokens. The resulting tokens are what the thought process reads and updates.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before it is windowed

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the comparison; its 1.129 million parameters make it the second largest of the five listed methods.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1, the second largest among CARN, IMDN, RFDN, CATANet, and DQ-CTM-SR.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison does not support calling DQ-CTM-SR cheap. CATANet is the smallest listed model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN and IMDN remain below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR is 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger still at 1.592 million parameters.
